newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: Search begins for missing Guatemalan rebel.
newsitem.headline: Search begins for missing Guatemalan rebel.

text.p: A criminal court judge and human rights activists searched the headquarters of the Guatemalan Presidential Guard on Friday but failed to find a trace of the missing rebel known as Mincho.
"Right now we're proving that he is not disappeared, he is dead," said human rights activist Karen Fischer, a member of the Alliance Against Impunity that petitioned the search.

The organisation won a court order against Gen. Marco Tulio Espinoza, chief of the Presidential Guard, to allow the search. The elite army corps is the main suspect in last year's disappearance of Juan Jose Cabrera Rodas, alias Mincho.
Judge Jorge Isaias Figueroa accompanied representatives of the alliance and public prosecutors on an all-day tour of Presidential Guard installations.
The search turned up no evidence of Cabrera, but was designed to pressure the Public Ministry into prosecuting those responsible for his disappearance, Fischer said.
It was the latest turn in this national mystery, which continued to generate daily headlines and public posturing.

Last week the United Nations Mission for the Verification of Human Rights in Guatemala (MINUGUA) concluded that Cabrera was captured and probably killed by government security forces last October for his involvement in a high-profile kidnapping of the matriarch of a wealthy Guatemalan family.

The MINUGUA report named the Presidential Guard, saying it operated as an illegal clandestine security force. On Friday MINUGUA representatives accompanied the delegation but did not enter the buildings being searched.

This week MINUGUA itself became the subject of an investigation by a team from the U.N.'s New York headquarters. At the request of MINUGUA Chief Jean Arnualt, two investigators arrived on Wednesday to look into accusations that Arnault helped cover up Cabrera's disappearance in order to protect the delicate peace process.

Arnault, a French diplomat, mediated the peace talks between the government and the Guatemalan National Revolutionary Unit (URNG). On Dec. 29, the parties signed an historic peace agreement ending 36 years of civil war.

The kidnapping occurred in the final phase of those talks, violating the ceasefire and deeply embarrassed the URNG. In a rare show of unity, the government and the URNG consistently denied that Cabrera existed.
